A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 54 readable pages. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original gradient-consistency simulations, particle and latent-angle experiments, and pretrained-model evaluation and controlled fine-tuning on MS-COCO.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain those original synthetic experiments and MS-COCO evaluation and fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: The unimodal and symmetric multimodal InfoNCE objectives, experimental encoders, particle objective, and optimization procedures remain unchanged. Revisions to intrinsic density constraints concern the theoretical analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture data, spherical two-well experiment, latent-angle misalignment scenarios, and MS-COCO pretrained-evaluation and caption-corruption tasks.

E2.justification: The Gibbs reference in the particle experiment, nine OpenCLIP checkpoints in Table 2, and RN50/ViT-B-16 corruption comparisons are retained. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Experimental settings match in v2 Appendix F and v3 Appendix E. These include the synthetic sweeps, evaluation metrics, first 5,000 MS-COCO validation images with up to five captions each, and 5,000-step projection-head/logit-scale fine-tuning with batch size 256.

E4.justification: Temperature concentration, controlled angular misalignment, caption corruption, and polar-marginal, joint-angle, residual-angle, and directional-retrieval analyses are retained. Matching the appendices establishes that their relocation introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain the 20-seed synthetic studies, Figure 3's mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and the multimodal gap's mean-and-standard-error reporting over seeds 0–19. No uncertainty procedure or repeated-run information changes.

E6.justification: Figures 2–12 retain their empirical results, and Table 2 retains all rows and values. For example, ResNet-50 image-to-text/text-to-image R@1 remains 0.480/0.289, with centroid gap 0.849. The caption-corruption results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 substantially revises the parametric-inheritance guarantee: v2 Corollary C.1 becomes Corollary B.1 with temperature-dependent optimizer sequences, explicitly vanishing approximation errors along those sequences, and concentration conditional on the corresponding Gibbs sequence concentrating. Its proof is revised accordingly. V3 also corrects Equation (28) from F + log Z = tau times KL to F + log Z = KL and introduces modality-specific density floors in Definition 4.3.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain large-batch value/gradient consistency, intrinsic unimodal Gibbs geometry with entropy as a tie-breaker, and negative symmetric divergence coupling that can sustain a multimodal gap. The conclusion still motivates controlling marginal divergence beyond pairwise alignment.

C2.justification: V3 expands v2's brief applicability caveats. Appendix A explains boundary-dependent kernel volume, while Appendix F.1 discusses how finite batches and temperatures may soften barriers, the difficulty of singular measures, and the distinction between objective geometry and actual optimization trajectories.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project-page address in a first-page footnote. Experimental implementation and hyperparameter documentation remain unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not establish what code or data the page hosts.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive positioning relative to alignment–uniformity, training dynamics, identifiability, and modality-gap research remain unchanged. Related work is condensed and moved into Section 6; bibliography and citation repairs do not introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and experimental narrative, revises section titles, moves related work from Appendix A into the main paper, and reorganizes the discussion into limitations and broader implications. The title, affiliations, publication header, and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and rearranged, with its caption explicitly identifying the landscapes as schematics. Other changes include relocated figures, revised captions and notation-table descriptions, and reflowed pages. The empirical graphics and result-table structure remain intact.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (28) and adding optimizer-sequence conditions in Corollary B.1 repair identifiable weaknesses in v2's reasoning. The expanded applicability discussion and reorganized narrative improve clarity. The net gain is limited: the central framework remains intact, and the newly introduced separate density floors are still inconsistently notated in Appendix D.2.
